answers.question: check whether the growth is organic and repeatable
answers.answer: Organic on its face (a growing order book, not acquisitions, is claimed) but not yet repeatable in the only sense that matters: the order book roughly doubled to ₹91,655L [business, page 207] while operating cash flow stayed negative all three years and ~30% of new sales is uncollected, so the growth is currently funded on paper, not proven in cash.

answers.question: veto — how is the business funded?
answers.answer: It is not funded by debt: total borrowings are negligible (₹232M latest, negative in prior years as printed), and net worth jumped from ₹4,957M to ₹15,678M, so the business is equity-funded — yet it still consumes cash (>₹9,700M cumulative FCF burn over three years). That means the IPO itself is likely the next funding round: the seller needs public money because internal accruals don't exist. On my own veto criteria (negative operating cash flow in all reported years with no document explanation), this fails.

The hard stop stands on what I was given.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A cash-flow or working-capital chapter showing a credible receivables recovery schedule (e.g., government dues with defined milestone collections) and a fresh-issue-vs-OFS split showing proceeds going into the business rather than exiting promoters.
